subsystems.name: EEG sensor array
subsystems.role: picks up the tiny voltage fluctuations produced by cortical activity.

subsystems.name: Stimulus delivery
subsystems.role: presents the same images or sounds to every user so responses can be compared.

subsystems.name: Signal acquisition
subsystems.role: amplifies, filters and digitises the microvolt-level signal.

subsystems.name: Feature extraction
subsystems.role: turns raw voltage traces into numbers that describe an individual's response.
parts: spectral power analysis (e.g. alpha, beta bands)

subsystems.name: Classifier and matcher
subsystems.role: decides whether a new recording belongs to an enrolled person.
parts: machine-learning model (e.g. support vector machine or neural network)

subsystems.name: Anti-spoofing and liveness
subsystems.role: checks the signal comes from a live person, not a recording or synthetic replay.

buildSteps.title: Design a stimulus protocol
buildSteps.detail: Choose a set of visual or auditory prompts that reliably evoke a distinctive brain response, such as the P300 wave, in every subject.

buildSteps.title: Collect enrolment recordings
buildSteps.detail: Record EEG from a user over several sessions, at different times of day and in different states, so the template captures natural variation.

buildSteps.title: Preprocess the signals
buildSteps.detail: Filter out mains interference, remove eye-blink and muscle artifacts, and cut the continuous data into short epochs aligned to each stimulus.

buildSteps.title: Extract discriminative features
buildSteps.detail: Compute averaged event-related potentials, band-power ratios and cross-electrode correlations for each stimulus type.

buildSteps.title: Train a classifier
buildSteps.detail: Use the enrolled users' features to train a model that separates one person's patterns from everyone else's, while keeping the model small enough for real-time use.

buildSteps.title: Validate across sessions
buildSteps.detail: Test the model on recordings taken weeks or months later to measure false-accept and false-reject rates, not just within-session accuracy.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with access control
buildSteps.detail: Embed the matcher in a door or workstation controller, add liveness checks, and store templates in a protected form rather than as raw brain data.

buildSteps.title: Operate and adapt
buildSteps.detail: Continuously monitor template drift and re-enrol when a user's signatures change with age, medication or fatigue.

prerequisites.why: gel electrodes work well but are impractical for daily access control; dry versions exist but are noisier and less stable.
eye blinks, jaw clenching and movement easily swamp the weak neural signal and must be removed automatically.

prerequisites.tech: Machine learning for small, noisy datasets
prerequisites.why: enrolment data per person is limited, so classifiers must generalise without overfitting.
EEG patterns shift with alertness, caffeine, sleep and age, which erodes accuracy between enrolment and later use.
brain-derived templates are sensitive personal data and need the same cryptographic protection as fingerprints.

pathway.milestone: laboratory studies reach high accuracy on small groups with many repeated trials
pathway.unlocks: proof that individuals can be distinguished from brief EEG recordings.

pathway.milestone: multi-session field trials with dry headsets and short enrolment
pathway.unlocks: realistic false-accept and false-reject figures for access control.

pathway.milestone: fusion with fingerprint or face recognition
pathway.unlocks: higher security by combining a neural check with an established biometric.
passive, ongoing identity checks for high-security rooms and systems without interrupting the user.
